questions.question: According to Archimedes’ principle, what is the magnitude of the upward force (buoyant force)?

options.text: It is equal to the pressure exerted by the fluid.
It is equal to the volume of the fluid.
It is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the body.
It is equal to the weight of the immersed body.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the body**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Archimedes' principle** states that when a body is immersed fully or partially in a **fluid**, it experiences an upward force that is equal to the **weight of the fluid displaced** by it.
 
• The upward force mentioned in the principle is known as the **buoyant force** or **upthrust**.
 
• The magnitude of this force depends on the **density of the fluid** and the **volume of the immersed part** of the body. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• While **pressure** exerted by the fluid increases with depth and contributes to the upward force (due to the pressure difference between the top and bottom of the object), the force itself is not numerically equal to the pressure. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The magnitude of the force is equal to the **weight** (a force measured in **Newtons**), not the **volume** (measured in **cubic meters**). Volume determines how much fluid is moved, but the force is the weight of that volume. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **weight of the immersed body** only equals the buoyant force when the object is **floating** in equilibrium. If the object sinks, its weight is greater than the buoyant force. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Buoyancy:** It is the property of a fluid to exert an upward force on any object immersed in it. This phenomenon is why objects feel lighter when submerged in **water**.
 
• **Density:** It is defined as the **mass per unit volume** of a substance. The **SI unit** of density is **kg/m³**. An object will float if its density is less than the density of the liquid.
 
• **Relative Density:** This is the ratio of the density of a substance to the density of **water** at **4 degrees Celsius**. Since it is a ratio of similar quantities, it has **no units**.
 
• **Applications of Archimedes' Principle:**
 
 
• **Designing Ships and Submarines:** Used to ensure they displace enough water to stay afloat or submerge as needed.
 
• **Lactometers:** These instruments are used to determine the **purity of a sample of milk** based on its density.
 
• **Hydrometers:** These are used for determining the **density of liquids**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Apparent Weight:** When an object is in a fluid, its **apparent weight** is its actual weight minus the **buoyant force**. This explains why heavy stones are easier to lift while they are still under the water.
 
• **Sinking vs. Floating:**
 
 
• If the **buoyant force** is less than the weight of the object, the object will **sink**.
 
• If the **buoyant force** is equal to or greater than the weight of the object, the object will **float**.
 
 
 
• The principle applies to all **fluids**, which include both **liquids** and **gases**. For example, a **hot air balloon** rises because the weight of the air it displaces is greater than the weight of the balloon itself.
 
• The discovery is attributed to **Archimedes**, a Greek mathematician and inventor from **Syracuse**, in the **3rd century BC**.

questions.question: In some reptiles, the sex of the offspring is determined by:

options.text: Temperature at which eggs are incubated
Presence or absence of a Y chromosome

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Temperature at which eggs are incubated**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In many **reptiles**, the sex of the offspring is not determined by **sex chromosomes** at the time of fertilization, but rather by the **environmental temperature** during **egg incubation**. This biological phenomenon is known as **Temperature-dependent Sex Determination (TSD)**.
 
• This process occurs during a specific window of **embryonic development** known as the **thermosensitive period (TSP)**. This period typically falls within the **middle third** of the total incubation time.
 
• The temperature experienced by the **developing embryo** during the **TSP** triggers physiological changes that determine whether the **gonads** will develop into **testes** or **ovaries**. ***Hence, the statement regarding temperature at which eggs are incubated is correct.***
 
• While most **mammals** and **birds** rely on **Genotypic Sex Determination (GSD)** involving **X, Y** or **Z, W chromosomes**, **TSD** is prevalent among various species of **turtles**, **crocodilians** (alligators and crocodiles), **tuataras**, and some species of **lizards**.
 
• Unlike **GSD**, where the sex ratio is usually **50:50**, **TSD** can lead to highly skewed sex ratios in a population depending on the **nesting environment** and **seasonal temperatures**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of TSD Patterns:**

 
 
• **Pattern Ia (MF):** In many **turtles**, **lower temperatures** during incubation produce **males**, while **higher temperatures** produce **females**.
 
• **Pattern Ib (FM):** In some **lizards** and **crocodilians**, the pattern is reversed, where **lower temperatures** result in **females** and **higher temperatures** result in **males**.
 
• **Pattern II (FMF):** In some species like **snapping turtles** and **crocodiles**, **females** are produced at both **extreme low and extreme high temperatures**, while **males** are produced at **intermediate temperatures**.
 
 
 
• **Biological Mechanism:**
 
 
• The conversion of **androgens** into **estrogens** is mediated by the enzyme **aromatase**. In species with **TSD**, the activity of this **enzyme** is often **temperature-sensitive**. **High temperatures** in certain species increase **aromatase activity**, leading to **ovary development** and **female offspring**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with GSD:**
 
 
• In **Genotypic Sex Determination (GSD)**, sex is fixed by **DNA**. For example, in **humans**, the presence of the **Y chromosome** (specifically the **SRY gene**) determines **maleness**. In some **reptiles** like **snakes**, **GSD** is the primary method, often using the **ZZ/ZW system** where **females** are the **heterogametic sex (ZW)**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental and Evolutionary Impact:**
 
 
• **Climate change** poses a significant threat to species with **TSD**. Rising **global temperatures** can lead to an **overproduction of one sex** (e.g., nearly all **female sea turtles**), which could eventually lead to **population collapse** due to a lack of **reproductive partners**.
 
• **Ecological factors** such as **nest depth**, **shading from vegetation**, and **soil moisture** also play critical roles in regulating the **incubation temperature** within the **nest**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **pivotal temperature** is defined as the specific **incubation temperature** that produces an **equal ratio (50%)** of **males and females**. Even a small change of **1-2 degrees Celsius** can completely flip the **sex ratio** of a clutch.
 
• It is important to note that **hormonal levels in the mother** do not directly determine the **genomic or environmental sex** of the offspring in the same way **incubation temperature** does, although they can influence **egg quality**.
 
• **Reptiles** like **Green Sea Turtles** are classic examples where **warming sands** due to **global warming** are currently resulting in **extreme female bias** in hatchlings.

questions.question: Which of the following nutrients in plants is generally supplied by soil?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Boron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Plants require various **essential nutrients** for their growth, metabolism, and reproductive cycles, which are categorized based on the quantity required into **macronutrients** and **micronutrients**.
 
• **Oxygen** is primarily obtained by plants from the **atmosphere** during respiration and is also derived from **water** during the process of **photosynthesis**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Hydrogen** is derived almost exclusively from **water** (**H2O**) absorbed by the roots from the environment. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Carbon** is taken up by plants from the **atmosphere** in the form of **carbon dioxide** (**CO2**) to build organic molecules through carbon fixation. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Boron** is a vital **mineral micronutrient** that is generally supplied to the plant by the **soil**. It is absorbed by plant roots primarily in the form of **undissociated boric acid**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Nutrients:**

 
 
• **Mineral Nutrients**: These are elements like **Nitrogen (N)**, **Phosphorus (P)**, **Potassium (K)**, **Calcium (Ca)**, **Magnesium (Mg)**, and **Sulfur (S)**, along with micronutrients like **Iron (Fe)** and **Boron (B)**, which are primarily sourced from the **soil**.
 
• **Non-Mineral Nutrients**: These include **Carbon**, **Hydrogen**, and **Oxygen**. They are considered non-mineral because they are supplied by **air and water** rather than soil minerals.
 
 
 
• **Role of Boron in Plants:**
 
 
• **Boron** is essential for **cell wall formation** and maintaining the structural integrity of **plasma membranes**.
 
• It plays a critical role in **reproductive growth**, specifically facilitating **pollen germination** and **pollen tube growth**.
 
• It is also involved in **sugar transport** and **calcium utilization** within the plant tissues.
 
 
 
• **Micronutrients from Soil:**
 
 
• Apart from **Boron**, other micronutrients supplied by the soil include **Manganese (Mn)**, **Copper (Cu)**, **Molybdenum (Mo)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, **Iron (Fe)**, **Chlorine (Cl)**, and **Nickel (Ni)**.
 
• These elements are required in very small quantities, typically less than **10 mmole per kg** of dry matter, but their deficiency can lead to significant physiological disorders.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nutrient Uptake Mechanism:**

 
 
• Plants absorb mineral nutrients from the **soil solution** through their **root hairs**. This process involves both **passive transport** (diffusion) and **active transport** (utilizing **ATP** energy).
 
• The availability of **Boron** in the soil is highly dependent on the **soil pH**; it is most readily available to plants in **acidic to neutral soils** (pH 5.0 to 7.0).
 
 
 
• **Source Summary:**
 
 
• **Air** provides **Carbon** and **Oxygen**.
 
• **Water** provides **Hydrogen** and **Oxygen**.
 
• **Soil** provides all other **13 essential mineral nutrients**, including **Nitrogen**, **Phosphorus**, and **Boron**.

questions.question: Which property is shown by ethanol?

options.text: It has a sweet smell and is volatile
It forms scum with hard water
It is solid at room temperature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It has a sweet smell and is volatile**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ethanol**, also known as **ethyl alcohol**, is a colorless liquid that possesses a distinct, **pleasant sweet smell** and a characteristic burning taste.
 
• It is a highly **volatile** substance, which means it evaporates rapidly at **standard temperature and pressure** due to its relatively low **boiling point** of **78.37°C** (**351.5 K**). ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The formation of **scum** (insoluble precipitates) is a property of **soap** reacting with **calcium** and **magnesium ions** in **hard water**. **Ethanol** is a covalent organic compound and does not react with these ions to form scum. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Ethanol** has a very low **melting point** of **-114.1°C** (**159 K**). Consequently, it exists in a **liquid state** at **room temperature** (approx **25°C**) and does not solidify under normal environmental conditions. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Chemically, **ethanol** is **neutral** in nature. Although its formula **C2H5OH** contains a **hydroxyl group**, it does not ionize in water to release **hydroxide ions** (OH-), nor does it change the color of **litmus paper**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is It has a sweet smell and is volatile.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Nature and Formula**: **Ethanol** is a **primary alcohol** with the chemical formula **C2H5OH**. It is the second member of the **homologous series** of alcohols.
 
• **Solubility**: It is **highly soluble** in **water** in all proportions. This solubility is due to the ability of the **hydroxyl group** in ethanol to form **hydrogen bonds** with **water molecules**.
 
• **Combustion**: It is a **flammable** liquid that burns with a clean **blue flame**. The reaction produces **carbon dioxide** and **water vapor**, releasing a significant amount of **energy**.
 
• **Applications as Fuel**: Because it is a **renewable** source of energy (often produced from **biomass**), it is used as an **additive in petrol**. In **India**, the **Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme** aims to increase the blend percentage to **20%** (**E20**) by the **year 2025**.
 
• **Industrial Uses**: It serves as a versatile **solvent** in the manufacture of **paints**, **varnishes**, **perfumes**, and **medicines** like **tincture of iodine** and **cough syrups**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reaction with Sodium**: When **ethanol** reacts with **sodium metal**, it evolves **hydrogen gas** and forms **sodium ethoxide**. This reaction is often used as a **chemical test** for the presence of the **alcoholic group**.
 
• **Oxidation**: Upon heating with **alkaline potassium permanganate** or **acidified potassium dichromate**, ethanol undergoes **oxidation** to form **ethanoic acid** (**acetic acid**).
 
• **Denatured Alcohol**: To prevent the **illegal consumption** of industrial-grade ethanol, it is made unfit for drinking by adding poisonous substances like **methanol** or **pyridine** and dyes like **copper sulphate** to give it a blue color. This is known as **denaturation**.
 
• **Medical Use**: In a concentration of **70%**, it is an effective **antiseptic** used in **hand sanitizers** to kill **microorganisms** by denaturing their **proteins** and dissolving their **lipid membranes**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about an object in non-uniform motion?

options.text: The change in velocity is zero over time interval
It moves unequal distances in unequal time intervals
It has different speeds at different points

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The change in velocity is zero over time interval**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-uniform motion** is defined as the motion of an object in which the object travels with **varied speed** and does not cover the same distance in equal time intervals.
 
• In **non-uniform motion**, the **velocity** of the object does not remain constant. Since velocity is a **vector quantity**, it changes if either the **speed** (magnitude) or the **direction** of motion changes.
 
• The statement "The change in velocity is zero over time interval" implies that the **initial velocity** and **final velocity** are identical, which means the **acceleration** is zero. This is a characteristic of **Uniform Motion**, not non-uniform motion. ***Hence, statement 1 is NOT true.***
 
• An object in non-uniform motion covers **unequal distances** in **equal intervals of time**. By extension, the relationship between distance and time is not linear, meaning it can move unequal distances in unequal time intervals depending on the **rate of acceleration**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct in the context of non-uniformity.***
 
• Because the rate of motion is constantly fluctuating, the object will possess **different speeds** at different points or instances along its path. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The core definition of non-uniform motion is that the **velocity changes with time**. This change indicates the presence of **acceleration** (positive or negative). ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration**: In **non-uniform motion**, the **acceleration** of the body is **non-zero**. Acceleration is the measure of the **rate of change of velocity** with respect to **time**. If the velocity increases, it is called acceleration; if it decreases, it is called **retardation** or **deceleration**.
 
• **Types of Non-Uniform Motion**:
 
 
• **Uniformly Accelerated Motion**: The velocity changes by **equal amounts** in equal intervals of time (e.g., a ball rolling down an inclined plane).
 
• **Non-uniformly Accelerated Motion**: The velocity changes by **unequal amounts** in equal intervals of time (e.g., a car moving in heavy city traffic).
 
 
 
• **Average Speed**: For an object in non-uniform motion, the **average speed** is calculated by dividing the **total distance** traveled by the **total time taken**. Unlike uniform motion, the **instantaneous speed** at any given point is usually different from the average speed.
 
• **Examples**: Common real-world examples include a **train** pulling out of a station, a **person jogging** in a crowded park, or a **pendulum** swinging back and forth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Graphical Representation**:

 
 
• In a **Distance-Time Graph**, non-uniform motion is represented by a **curved line** (parabola or zig-zag), indicating that the **slope** (speed) is changing.
 
• In a **Velocity-Time Graph**, non-uniform motion is represented by any line that is **not horizontal**. A horizontal line would indicate constant velocity (uniform motion).
 
 
 
• **Uniform Motion vs. Non-Uniform Motion**:
 
 
• **Uniform Motion**: Covers equal distance in equal time; **zero acceleration**; **constant velocity**.
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion**: Covers unequal distance in equal time; **variable acceleration**; **changing velocity**.
 
 
 
• **Directional Change**: It is important to note that even if an object moves at a **constant speed** in a circle (**Uniform Circular Motion**), it is considered **non-uniform motion** because its **direction** is constantly changing, resulting in a change in **velocity**.

questions.question: Xylem is a complex permanent tissue. Which of the following is correct regarding its composition?

options.text: Tracheids, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres
Companion cells, tracheids and xylem fibres
Vessels, xylem collenchyma and xylem fibres
Tracheids, sieve cells and phloem parenchyma

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tracheids, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem** is defined as a **complex permanent tissue** in plants, primarily responsible for the **conduction of water and dissolved minerals** from the roots to the rest of the plant parts.
 
• It is termed a **complex tissue** because it consists of more than one type of cell that coordinates to perform a common function. The four main components of xylem in **angiosperms** are **Tracheids, Vessels, Xylem Parenchyma, and Xylem Fibres**.
 
• **Tracheids, xylem parenchyma, and xylem fibres** are all integral parts of the xylem tissue. While **vessels** are also a key component in **flowering plants**, the provided option correctly identifies three valid xylem constituents. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Companion cells** are a component of **Phloem**, not xylem. They help in the loading and unloading of sugars into sieve tubes. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Collenchyma** is a **simple permanent tissue** that provides mechanical support to young stems and petioles; it is not a sub-type of xylem tissue. Xylem has its own supporting tissue known as **Xylem Fibres** (or sclerenchyma). ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Sieve cells** and **phloem parenchyma** are specialized cells belonging to the **Phloem**, which is the vascular tissue responsible for transporting **organic nutrients (food)**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Components of Xylem:**

 
 
• **Tracheids:** These are **elongated, tube-like dead cells** with thick, **lignified walls** and tapering ends. They are the primary water-conducting elements in **Gymnosperms** and lower vascular plants.
 
• **Vessels:** Long, cylindrical structures formed by several cells called **vessel members**. They have **perforated end walls** and are much more efficient at water transport than tracheids. They are characteristic features of **Angiosperms**.
 
• **Xylem Parenchyma:** These are the only **living cells** in the xylem tissue. They have thin **cellulosic walls** and function mainly in the **storage of food** (starch or fat) and the **lateral conduction** of water.
 
• **Xylem Fibres:** These are **dead cells** with highly thickened **lignified walls** and obliterated central lumens. Their primary function is to provide **mechanical strength and support** to the plant body.
 
 
 
• **Direction of Flow:** Unlike phloem, which exhibits **bidirectional transport**, the flow in xylem is strictly **unidirectional** (from roots upwards to the leaves).
 
• **Wood:** In botanical terms, the **secondary xylem** produced during the **secondary growth** of a plant is what we commonly refer to as **wood**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolutionary Fact:** In **Gymnosperms** (like pines and cedars), **vessels are absent**; water is conducted almost entirely through **tracheids**.
 
• **Primary Xylem:** It is categorized into **Protoxylem** (first formed) and **Metaxylem** (later formed). In stems, the protoxylem lies towards the center (**Endarch condition**), while in roots, it lies towards the periphery (**Exarch condition**).
 
• **Lignification:** The deposition of **lignin** in the cell walls of tracheids and vessels provides the structural rigidity necessary to withstand the **negative pressure** generated during **transpiration**.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is correct regarding 'property of Gaseous state'?

options.text: In gaseous state, intermolecular attraction and intermolecular distance are very large
In gaseous state, intermolecular distance is very low and intermolecular attraction is very large.
In gaseous state, intermolecular distance is very large and intermolecular attraction is very low.
In gaseous state, intermolecular distance and intermolecular attraction are very low.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In gaseous state, intermolecular distance is very large and intermolecular attraction is very low.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Matter exists in three primary physical states: **Solid**, **Liquid**, and **Gas**. The state of matter is determined by the balance between **intermolecular forces** and **thermal energy**.
 
• In the **gaseous state**, the particles (atoms or molecules) possess high **kinetic energy**, which overcomes the forces of attraction between them.
 
• The **intermolecular distance** in gases is **very large**. In fact, the distance between gas molecules is much greater than the actual size of the molecules themselves. ***Hence, the statement regarding large intermolecular distance is correct.***
 
• The **intermolecular attraction** (cohesive forces) between gas particles is **very low** or negligible. This lack of attraction allows gas particles to move independently and expand to fill any container. ***Hence, the statement regarding low intermolecular attraction is correct.***
 
• Regarding the other options:
 
 
• Statement 1 suggests both distance and attraction are very large; this is contradictory as large distance usually results in weak attraction. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 2 describes the **Solid state**, where particles are close together (low distance) and strongly bonded (large attraction). ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 4 suggests both distance and attraction are very low; while attraction is low, the distance is actually very high in gases. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Gases:**

 
 
• **Compressibility:** Due to the **large intermolecular distances**, gases are **highly compressible**. Applying pressure reduces the empty space between molecules.
 
• **Shape and Volume:** Gases have **no definite shape** and **no definite volume**. They take the shape and volume of the container they occupy.
 
• **Diffusion:** Because of **weak intermolecular forces** and **high speed** of particles, gases diffuse very rapidly into each other.
 
• **Density:** Gases have **very low density** compared to solids and liquids because the same mass occupies a much larger volume.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Molecular Theory (KMT):**
 
 
• This theory explains that gas particles are in **constant, random motion**.
 
• The collisions between gas particles and the walls of the container are **perfectly elastic**, which exerts **pressure**.
 
• The **average kinetic energy** of the particles is directly proportional to the **absolute temperature** (measured in **Kelvin**).
 
 
 
• **Comparison with other states:**
 
 
• **Solids:** Have **fixed shape and volume**, **strongest intermolecular forces**, and **minimum intermolecular space**.
 
• **Liquids:** Have **fixed volume but no fixed shape**, **intermediate intermolecular forces**, and **moderate intermolecular space** compared to gases.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Van der Waals Forces:** In real gases, there are slight **attractive forces** known as **Van der Waals forces**. However, in an **Ideal Gas** model, these attractions are assumed to be **zero**.
 
• **Boyle's Law:** States that at **constant temperature**, the **volume** of a gas is inversely proportional to its **pressure** ($P \propto 1/V$).
 
• **Charles's Law:** States that at **constant pressure**, the **volume** of a gas is directly proportional to its **absolute temperature** ($V \propto T$).
 
• The transition from liquid to gas is called **vaporization** or **boiling**, which occurs when **thermal energy** is sufficient to break the **intermolecular attractions** of the liquid phase.

questions.question: A metallic conductor obeys Ohm’s law at room temperature. When the applied potential difference across it is increased from V to 2V, and the temperature is kept constant, the current through the conductor:

options.text: Remains unchanged because current depends only on resistance
More than doubles due to increased electron drift velocity
Less than doubles due to heating effects

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Doubles because resistance is constant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ohm’s Law** states that the current (**I**) flowing through a metallic conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference (**V**) applied across its ends, provided its physical conditions such as **temperature** remain constant.
 
• The mathematical expression for this relationship is **V = I * R**, where **R** represents the **Electrical Resistance** of the conductor.
 
• In this scenario, since the **temperature is kept constant**, the resistance (**R**) of the metallic conductor remains unchanged regardless of the change in voltage.
 
• When the potential difference is increased from **V** to **2V**, the new current (**I'**) can be calculated using the formula **I' = (2V) / R**. Since **I = V / R**, it follows that **I' = 2 * I**.
 
• The current **doubles** because it maintains a **linear relationship** with the potential difference in an ohmic conductor. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Statement 1 is incorrect because while current does depend on resistance, it is also a function of the applied **potential difference**.
 
• Statement 3 is incorrect because at a constant temperature, the **drift velocity** of electrons increases proportionally with the electric field (and thus voltage), leading exactly to a doubling of current, not "more than double."
 
• Statement 4 is incorrect because the question explicitly specifies that the **temperature is kept constant**, which implies any **heating effects** (Joule heating) are either neglected or compensated for to keep **R** stable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electrical Resistance (R):** It is the property of a material to oppose the flow of **electric current**. The **SI unit** of resistance is the **Ohm** (represented by the Greek letter **Ω**).
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance:** The resistance of a conductor depends on its **length** (directly proportional), **area of cross-section** (inversely proportional), the **nature of the material** (resistivity), and **temperature**.
 
• **Drift Velocity:** This is the average velocity attained by **charged particles** (such as electrons) in a material due to an **electric field**. The current (**I**) is defined as **I = n * A * e * Vd**, where **Vd** is the drift velocity. Since **Vd** is proportional to **V**, current is also proportional to **V**.
 
• **Ohmic and Non-Ohmic Devices:**
 
 
• **Ohmic Conductors:** Materials like **Copper**, **Silver**, and **Aluminum** that follow Ohm's law, showing a straight-line **V-I graph** passing through the origin.
 
• **Non-Ohmic Conductors:** Devices like **semiconductors**, **diodes**, and **transistors** where the resistance changes as the voltage or current changes, resulting in a non-linear **V-I characteristic**.
 
 
 
• **Temperature Coefficient:** For pure metals, resistance increases with an increase in **temperature**. This is because the thermal vibrations of metal ions increase, leading to more frequent collisions with **drifting electrons**. However, in this specific problem, the constant temperature constraint ensures **Ohm's Law** is strictly followed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ohm's Law Discovery:** The law was named after the German physicist **Georg Simon Ohm**, who published his findings in **1827**.
 
• **Power Dissipation:** When current flows through a resistor, electrical energy is converted into heat. This is known as **Joule Heating**, given by **P = I² * R** or **P = V² / R**. In real-world applications, if the voltage doubles, the power dissipation increases **four times**, which would normally raise the temperature unless cooled.
 
• **Conductance:** The reciprocal of resistance is called **conductance (G)**, measured in **Siemens (S)** or **mho**. **G = 1 / R**.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of basic salt?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium bicarbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3)**, commonly known as **baking soda**, is a **basic salt**. It is formed by the neutralization reaction between a **strong base**, **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**, and a **weak acid**, **Carbonic acid (H2CO3)**. Since the base is stronger than the acid, the resulting salt retains basic characteristics.
 
• **Sodium chloride (NaCl)** is a **neutral salt**. It is produced from the reaction of **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**, which is a **strong base**, and **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)**, which is a **strong acid**. In an aqueous solution, it typically maintains a **pH** of around **7**.
 
• **Ammonium chloride (NH4Cl)** is an example of an **acidic salt**. It is formed through the reaction of a **strong acid**, **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)**, and a **weak base**, **Ammonium hydroxide (NH4OH)**. Due to the dominance of the strong acid, the salt exhibits acidic properties in water.
 
• **Hydrogen chloride (HCl)** is not a salt at all; it is a **strong mineral acid**. In its gaseous form, it is hydrogen chloride, and when dissolved in water, it becomes **hydrochloric acid**, which is highly corrosive and has a very low **pH**.
 
• A **basic salt** is generally defined as a salt that reacts with water to produce a solution with a **pH greater than 7**. This occurs because the **anion** of the weak acid undergoes **hydrolysis** to produce **hydroxide ions (OH-)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Nature of Salts**:

 
 
• **Neutral Salts**: Formed from a **strong acid and a strong base** (e.g., **KNO3**, **NaCl**).
 
• **Acidic Salts**: Formed from a **strong acid and a weak base** (e.g., **(NH4)2SO4**, **NH4Cl**).
 
• **Basic Salts**: Formed from a **weak acid and a strong base** (e.g., **CH3COONa**, **Na2CO3**).
 
 
 
• **Properties of Sodium Bicarbonate**:
 
 
• It is a **white crystalline solid** but often appears as a fine powder.
 
• It has a slightly **salty, alkaline taste**.
 
• The **pH** of a **0.1 M** solution of **Sodium bicarbonate** is approximately **8.3** at **25 degrees Celsius**.
 
 
 
• **Applications**:
 
 
• **Baking**: It reacts with acidic components in batters to release **Carbon dioxide (CO2)**, causing the dough to rise.
 
• **Medical**: Used as an **antacid** to treat **acid indigestion** and **heartburn** by neutralizing excess stomach acid.
 
• **Industrial**: Used in **soda-acid fire extinguishers** and as a mild **abrasive** in cleaning products.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Salt Hydrolysis**: This is the process where the salt reacts with water to give back the acid and base. In the case of **Sodium bicarbonate**, the **bicarbonate ion (HCO3-)** reacts with water to form **undissociated carbonic acid** and **hydroxide ions**, leading to **alkalinity**.
 
• **Solubility**: **Sodium bicarbonate** is **sparingly soluble** in water compared to other sodium salts, but its solubility increases with **temperature**.
 
• **Safety and Storage**: While generally safe, it should be stored in a **cool, dry place** as moisture can cause it to clump or lose its leavening effectiveness over time.

questions.question: Which of the following allotropes of carbon conducts electricity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Graphite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Graphite** is a crystalline **allotrope of carbon** that is widely recognized for its ability to **conduct electricity**, which is an exception among non-metals.
 
• In the structure of graphite, each carbon atom is covalently bonded to **three other carbon atoms** in the same plane, creating a series of **hexagonal rings** arranged in layers.
 
• The carbon atoms in graphite undergo **sp2 hybridization**. This leaves **one valence electron** per carbon atom unbonded and "free" within the layers.
 
• These **delocalized electrons** are mobile and can move throughout the graphite sheet, allowing it to act as an efficient **electrical conductor**.
 
• Due to this property, graphite is extensively used in the production of **electrodes** in batteries and industrial **electrolysis** processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Diamond**:

 
 
• It is another major **allotrope of carbon** where each atom is bonded to **four other carbon atoms** in a rigid **tetrahedral structure**.
 
• This involves **sp3 hybridization**, meaning all **four valence electrons** are tightly held in **covalent bonds**.
 
• Because there are **no free or delocalized electrons**, diamond acts as an **electrical insulator**.
 
 
 
• **Fullerenes (C60)**:
 
 
• Discovered in **1985**, these are spherical allotropes of carbon, often called **Buckminsterfullerene** or buckyballs.
 
• While they possess **pi-electron systems**, pure fullerenes are generally **insulators** or **semiconductors** under normal conditions rather than conductors.
 
 
 
• **Charcoal**:
 
 
• This is an **amorphous allotrope** of carbon obtained by the **destructive distillation** of wood.
 
• Unlike graphite, its structure is highly **disordered and porous**, which prevents the effective flow of electrons, making it a **poor conductor** of electricity.
 
 
 
• **Allotropy**:
 
 
• This is the phenomenon where a single chemical element exists in **multiple physical forms** that differ in their **atomic arrangement**.
 
• Other allotropes of carbon include **graphene**, **carbon nanotubes**, and **coke**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lubrication**: Beyond conductivity, the **weak Van der Waals forces** between the hexagonal layers of graphite allow them to slide over each other, making it an excellent **dry lubricant**.
 
• **Thermal Stability**: Graphite has a very high **melting point** (above **3600 degrees Celsius**), which allows it to be used in high-temperature **crucibles** and **nuclear reactors** as a **neutron moderator**.
 
• **Comparison**: While **diamond** is the **hardest known natural substance** due to its 3D bonding, **graphite** is soft and slippery due to its 2D layered bonding.

questions.question: When we pour acetone (nail polish remover) on our palm, we feel cold because:

options.text: it blocks nerve signals on the skin
it evaporates rapidly, absorbing heat from the palm
it reacts with water present on the palm

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**it evaporates rapidly, absorbing heat from the palm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Evaporation** is a **surface phenomenon** where molecules in the liquid state gain enough energy to enter the gaseous state. This process inherently causes a **cooling effect** because the escaping high-energy molecules take thermal energy away from the surface.
 
• **Acetone**, commonly known as **nail polish remover**, is a highly **volatile liquid**. Volatile substances are those that have a high **vapor pressure** and a **low boiling point**, meaning they transition from liquid to vapor very easily at **room temperature**.
 
• When **acetone** is poured onto the palm, the molecules use the **latent heat of vaporization** required for the phase change. They absorb this necessary **thermal energy** directly from the **skin of the palm**. ***Hence, the statement that it evaporates rapidly, absorbing heat from the palm is correct.***
 
• As the **palm loses heat** to the acetone, the **temperature** of the skin surface drops. This physical change is detected by **thermoreceptors** (nerve endings) in the skin, which send signals to the brain, resulting in the sensation of **coldness**.
 
• Regarding the other options: **Statement 1** is incorrect as the cold sensation is due to heat loss from the hand, not the "release" of cold vapors. **Statement 2** is incorrect because acetone does not act as an **anesthetic** to block nerve signals in this context. **Statement 4** is incorrect because the effect is a **physical phase change**, not a **chemical reaction** with water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Latent Heat of Vaporization**: This is the amount of **heat energy** required to change **1 kg** of a liquid into a gas at its boiling point without any change in temperature. For acetone, this value is approximately **518 kJ/kg** at its boiling point.
 
• **Boiling Point of Acetone**: Acetone has a relatively low boiling point of about **56.05°C** (**329.2 K**) compared to water, which boils at **100°C**. This low boiling point is why it feels much colder than water when placed on the skin, as it **evaporates** much faster.
 
• **Intermolecular Forces**: The reason acetone is volatile is due to its **weak intermolecular forces**. While it has **dipole-dipole interactions**, it lacks the strong **hydrogen bonding** present in water, making it easier for acetone molecules to break away from the liquid surface.
 
• **Comparison with Alcohol**: Similar to acetone, **isopropyl alcohol** (rubbing alcohol) and **ethanol** also produce a cooling sensation. These are also volatile liquids frequently used in **sanitizers** and medical swabs.
 
• **Factors Affecting Evaporation**: The rate at which a liquid like acetone evaporates depends on the **surface area** (spreading it on the palm increases the rate), **temperature**, and **humidity**. Higher temperatures and lower humidity levels **accelerate** the evaporation process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chemical Formula**: Acetone is the simplest **ketone** with the chemical formula **(CH3)2CO**. It is a colorless, flammable liquid.
 
• **Industrial Uses**: Beyond **nail polish remover**, acetone is used as a **solvent** for plastics, synthetic fibers, and in the manufacture of **methyl methacrylate**.
 
• **Biological Context**: Small amounts of acetone are produced in the **human body** through **metabolic processes** (ketosis). Excessive levels can be found in the breath of individuals with **diabetes mellitus**.
 
• **Safety**: While it provides a cooling sensation, prolonged skin contact with acetone can cause **defatting** of the skin, leading to **irritation** or **dermatitis**, as it dissolves the natural oils present on the skin surface.

questions.question: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 {m/sec}² for 5 seconds. What is the velocity at the end of 5 seconds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 m/sec**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The problem involves a car moving with **uniform acceleration**, which allows the use of the **equations of motion** derived by **Sir Isaac Newton**.
 
• According to the question, the car starts from **rest**. In physics, when an object starts from rest, its **initial velocity (u)** is always considered to be **0 m/sec**.
 
• The **acceleration (a)** provided is **2 m/sec²**. This means the **velocity** of the car increases by **2 meters per second** every single second.
 
• The **time (t)** duration for which the acceleration is applied is **5 seconds**.
 
• To find the **final velocity (v)**, we use the **first equation of motion**: **v = u + at**.
 
• By substituting the given values: **v = 0 + (2 × 5)**. Therefore, **v = 10 m/sec**.
 
• The final **velocity** at the end of **5 seconds** is **10 m/sec**. ***Hence, the calculation confirms that the fourth option is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uniform Acceleration:**

 
 
• This occurs when the **velocity** of an object changes by an equal amount in every equal **time interval**.
 
• In a **Velocity-Time graph**, uniform acceleration is represented by a **straight line**. The **slope** of this line gives the value of the **acceleration**.
 
 
 
• **Equations of Motion:**
 
 
• There are three primary equations for **constant acceleration**:
 
 
• **v = u + at**: Relates velocity, acceleration, and time.
 
• **s = ut + ½at²**: Relates **displacement (s)**, initial velocity, time, and acceleration.
 
• **v² = u² + 2as**: Relates final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and displacement.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Scalar and Vector Quantities:**
 
 
• **Velocity** is a **vector quantity** because it has both **magnitude** and **direction**. Its **S.I. unit** is **m/s**.
 
• **Acceleration** is also a **vector quantity**, representing the rate of change of velocity. Its **S.I. unit** is **m/s²**.
 
• **Speed** is the **scalar** counterpart of velocity, representing only the magnitude of motion.
 
 
 
• **Real-world Application:**
 
 
• These kinematic equations are fundamental in **engineering** and **automotive safety** to calculate **braking distances** and **engine performance**. For example, if a car is **decelerating** (negative acceleration), the same formulas apply by using a **negative value** for **a**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Initial State:** Always identify if the object starts from **rest (u=0)** or comes to a **stop (v=0)**, as these are critical numerical cues in physics problems.
 
• **Units:** Ensure all parameters are in **S.I. units** (meters and seconds) before calculation. If the speed was given in **km/hr**, it would need to be multiplied by **5/18** to convert to **m/sec**.
 
• **Direction:** Since acceleration is a vector, if the **acceleration** is in the opposite direction of the **velocity**, it is termed **retardation** or **deceleration**, and its value is taken as **negative** in the equations.
 
• **Displacement Calculation:** If the question asked for the **distance** traveled in those **5 seconds**, we would use **s = ut + ½at²**, resulting in **s = 0 + ½(2)(5)² = 25 meters**.

questions.question: The metal which will NOT displace lead from its salt solution is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ability of one metal to displace another from its salt solution depends on the **Reactivity Series** of metals. This series ranks metals based on their chemical reactivity, primarily their ability to lose electrons and form **positive ions**.
 
• A **displacement reaction** is a type of chemical reaction where a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound. In the context of metals, a metal higher in the reactivity series will displace any metal placed below it from its aqueous salt solution.
 
• **Aluminium** is significantly more reactive than **Lead**. In the reactivity series, **Aluminium (Al)** is positioned much higher than **Lead (Pb)**. Therefore, if Aluminium is added to a lead salt solution, it will displace the lead. ***Hence, the statement regarding Aluminium is incorrect for this question.***
 
• **Calcium** and **Magnesium** are highly reactive metals belonging to the **Alkaline Earth Metals** group. Both **Calcium (Ca)** and **Magnesium (Mg)** sit high up in the reactivity series, well above **Lead (Pb)**. They can easily displace Lead from its salt solution. ***Hence, the statements regarding Calcium and Magnesium are incorrect for this question.***
 
• **Copper (Cu)** is placed below **Lead (Pb)** in the reactivity series. Since Copper is less reactive than Lead, it does not possess the chemical potential to displace Lead ions from a solution. ***Hence, the statement regarding Copper is correct as it will NOT displace lead.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Reactivity Series:**

 
 
• The series follows a general order: **Potassium (K)** > **Sodium (Na)** > **Calcium (Ca)** > **Magnesium (Mg)** > **Aluminium (Al)** > **Zinc (Zn)** > **Iron (Fe)** > **Tin (Sn)** > **Lead (Pb)** > **Hydrogen (H)** > **Copper (Cu)** > **Mercury (Hg)** > **Silver (Ag)** > **Gold (Au)**.
 
• Metals like **Potassium** and **Sodium** are so reactive they are often stored in **kerosene** to prevent reaction with moisture in the air.
 
• Metals at the bottom, such as **Gold** and **Platinum**, are known as **noble metals** because they are extremely unreactive and do not easily corrode or react with acids.
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reaction Mechanism:**
 
 
• In these reactions, the more reactive metal undergoes **oxidation** (loses electrons), while the less reactive metal ion in the solution undergoes **reduction** (gains electrons).
 
• For example, if **Magnesium** is put into **Lead Nitrate** solution, the Magnesium atoms turn into ions, and Lead ions turn into solid metallic Lead.
 
• Since **Copper** is lower than **Lead**, it cannot force its electrons onto Lead ions; therefore, no reaction occurs when Copper is placed in a Lead salt solution.
 
 
 
• **Lead (Pb):**
 
 
• **Lead** has the atomic number **82**. It is a heavy metal that is denser than most common materials.
 
• It is relatively resistant to corrosion but is placed above **Hydrogen** in the reactivity series, meaning it can theoretically displace hydrogen from dilute acids, though the reaction is often slowed by the formation of insoluble coatings.
 
 
 
• **Copper (Cu):**
 
 
• **Copper** has the atomic number **29**. It is a transition metal known for high **thermal and electrical conductivity**.
 
• It is one of the few metals that occur in nature in a directly usable metallic form (native metals). Because it is below **Hydrogen** and **Lead**, it is considered a relatively stable and unreactive metal in many environments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Electrochemical Context:** The reactivity series is fundamentally linked to **Standard Reduction Potentials**. Metals with a more negative reduction potential are more reactive and act as stronger **reducing agents**.
 
• **Practical Application:** This principle is used in **Galvanization**, where **Zinc** (more reactive) is used to coat **Iron** to prevent rusting. The Zinc displaces the corrosive action from the Iron by acting as a sacrificial anode.
 
• **Metal Extraction:** The reactivity of a metal determines the method used to extract it from its ore. Highly reactive metals like **Aluminium** are extracted via **electrolysis**, while less reactive metals like **Lead** or **Iron** can be extracted by reduction with **Carbon**.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics is correct about magnetic field lines?

options.text: They always start and end at the same pole.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They always form closed loops**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magnetic field lines** are imaginary lines used to represent the **magnetic field** around a magnet. They are continuous and form **closed loops**. Externally, they emerge from the **North pole** and enter the **South pole**, while internally, they travel from the **South pole** back to the **North pole**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• It is a fundamental property that magnetic field lines **never intersect** or cross each other. If they were to intersect at a certain point, it would imply that a **magnetic compass** placed at that point would show two different directions for the magnetic field simultaneously, which is **physically impossible**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Magnetic field lines do not start and end at the **same pole**. They exist as a continuous flow from the **North pole** to the **South pole** outside the magnet and complete the circuit inside. This distinguishes them from **electric field lines**, which can start on a positive charge and end on a negative charge. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Because magnetic poles always exist in **dipoles** (North and South), these field lines must return to their source, making them **closed curves** rather than **open curves**. There are no isolated magnetic **monopoles** in nature that would allow for open field lines. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is they always form closed loops.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Magnetic Field**:

 
 
• The **magnetic field** is a **vector quantity**, meaning it possesses both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
• The **SI unit** of magnetic field strength is the **Tesla (T)**, named after **Nikola Tesla**. Another common unit used is the **Gauss**, where **1 Tesla** equals **10,000 Gauss**.
 
 
 
• **Field Strength and Density**:
 
 
• The relative **strength** of the magnetic field is shown by the **degree of closeness** of the field lines.
 
• Where the lines are **crowded** (near the **poles**), the magnetic field is **strongest**. As the lines spread apart, the field becomes **weaker**.
 
 
 
• **Directionality**:
 
 
• The **tangent** drawn to a magnetic field line at any given point indicates the **direction** of the magnetic field at that specific location.
 
• The direction is determined by the way the **North pole** of a magnetic needle would point when placed in the field.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gauss's Law for Magnetism**: This law states that the net **magnetic flux** through any **closed surface** is always **zero**. This mathematical principle confirms that magnetic **monopoles** do not exist and that field lines must be **closed loops**.
 
• **Discovery**: The concept of **lines of force** or field lines was first introduced by the **19th-century** scientist **Michael Faraday** to visualize **electromagnetic induction** and magnetic interactions.
 
• **Earth's Magnetic Field**: The **Earth** acts as a giant **bar magnet**. Its magnetic field lines emerge from the **magnetic South Pole** (near the geographic North) and enter the **magnetic North Pole** (near the geographic South). This property is essential for **navigation** using a **magnetic compass**.
 
• **Solenoids**: In a current-carrying **solenoid**, the magnetic field pattern is remarkably similar to that of a **bar magnet**, where the lines form **parallel** and **uniform** paths inside the coil, reinforcing the concept of **closed loops**.

questions.question: An object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror. The image formed is:

options.text: At the centre of curvature, same size

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**At the centre of curvature, same size**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an **object** is placed at the **centre of curvature (C)** of a **concave mirror**, the light rays reflecting from the object converge at the same point **C**.
 
• According to the laws of reflection, a ray parallel to the **principal axis** passes through the **focus (F)** after reflection, and a ray passing through the focus becomes parallel to the principal axis.
 
• These reflected rays intersect exactly at the **centre of curvature**, forming the image at that location. ***Hence, the statement that the image is formed at the centre of curvature is correct.***
 
• The **nature** of the image formed in this specific case is **real and inverted** because the light rays actually meet at the point of image formation.
 
• The **size** of the image is **exactly the same** as the size of the object, which is a unique property of this position in concave mirrors. ***Hence, the correct answer is At the centre of curvature, same size.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror Characteristics**:

 
 
• A **concave mirror** is also known as a **converging mirror** because it tends to collect light that falls on it, refocusing parallel incoming rays to a single **focus**.
 
• It has a **reflective surface** that is curved inward, resembling a portion of the inner surface of a hollow **sphere**.
 
• The **uses** of concave mirrors include **shaving mirrors**, **dentist's mirrors** to see enlarged images of teeth, and **reflectors** in **car headlights** and **searchlights**.
 
 
 
• **Other Image Positions in Concave Mirrors**:
 
 
• **At Infinity**: If the object is at infinity, the image is formed at the **focus (F)** and is **highly diminished** and **point-sized**.
 
• **Beyond C**: When the object is beyond the **centre of curvature**, the image is formed **between F and C**, and it is **diminished** and **real**.
 
• **Between C and F**: If the object is placed between the centre of curvature and the focus, the image is formed **beyond C** and is **magnified**.
 
• **At Focus (F)**: When the object is at the focus, the image is formed at **infinity** and is **highly magnified**.
 
• **Between F and Pole (P)**: This is the only case where a **virtual and erect** image is formed **behind the mirror**, which is also **magnified**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mirror Formula**: The relationship between **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by the formula **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**.
 
• **Magnification (m)**: It is defined as the ratio of the **height of the image (h')** to the **height of the object (h)**, expressed as **m = h'/h = -v/u**. For an object at **C**, the magnification is **-1**, indicating a **same-sized**, **inverted** image.
 
• **Radius of Curvature (R)**: The distance from the **pole** to the **centre of curvature** is called the **radius of curvature**. In spherical mirrors, the **focal length** is exactly half of the radius of curvature (**f = R/2**).
 
• **Sign Convention**: According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the distances measured in the direction of incident light are positive, while those measured against it are negative. For a concave mirror, the **focal length** and **radius of curvature** are always **negative**.

questions.question: Which energy change is generally associated with decomposition reactions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Endothermic energy change**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Decomposition reactions** are chemical processes where a single reactant breaks down into two or more simpler products.
 
• For a decomposition reaction to occur, the **chemical bonds** within the reactant molecule must be broken. Breaking these bonds requires an **input of energy** from the external environment.
 
• Because these reactions involve the **absorption of energy** (in the form of heat, light, or electricity), they are generally characterized by an **Endothermic energy change**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• An **Exothermic energy change** is the opposite, where energy is released into the surroundings; this is typically seen in combination or combustion reactions rather than decomposition. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The general representation of this reaction is **AB + Energy → A + B**, indicating that the energy is a necessary "reactant" for the process to proceed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Decomposition Reactions:**

 
 
• **Thermal Decomposition**: This occurs when **heat energy** is utilized for the reaction. For example, when **Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3)** is heated, it decomposes into **Calcium Oxide (CaO)** and **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**. This process is vital in the **cement industry**.
 
• **Electrolytic Decomposition (Electrolysis)**: This involves passing an **electric current** through a compound in a liquid or molten state. A well-known example is the **electrolysis of water**, which decomposes **H2O** into **Hydrogen (H2)** and **Oxygen (O2)** gases.
 
• **Photolytic Decomposition (Photolysis)**: This is triggered by **light energy**. For instance, **Silver Chloride (AgCl)** turns grey in sunlight because it decomposes into **Silver metal** and **Chlorine gas**. This principle was historically used in **black and white photography**.
 
 
 
• **Energy Dynamics:**
 
 
• In an **Endothermic reaction**, the total energy of the products is higher than the total energy of the reactants because energy has been "stored" in the system during the reaction.
 
• In contrast, **Exothermic reactions** (like respiration or burning of natural gas) result in products with lower energy than the reactants, with the excess being released as **Heat**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Law of Conservation of Energy** states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed. In decomposition, **kinetic or thermal energy** from the environment is transformed into **chemical potential energy** within the products.
 
• **Activation Energy**: Even if a reaction is overall endothermic, it requires a specific amount of **activation energy** to initiate the bond-breaking process.
 
• **Digestive System**: In the human body, the **digestion of food** is a series of decomposition reactions where complex substances like carbohydrates and proteins are broken down into simpler molecules like **glucose** and **amino acids**, often aided by **enzymes**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an application of ultrasound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cooking food**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ultrasound** refers to sound waves with frequencies higher than the upper audible limit of human hearing, which is typically **20,000 Hz (20 kHz)**.
 
• **Cleaning delicate machinery parts**: This is a major application where objects like **electronic components**, **watch parts**, or **surgical instruments** are placed in a cleaning solution. High-frequency **ultrasound waves** are sent through the liquid, causing high-pressure bubbles to form and collapse (**cavitation**), which dislodges dust, grease, and dirt from hard-to-reach surfaces. ***Hence, this is a correct application.***
 
• **Detecting cracks and flaws in metal blocks**: In large constructions like **bridges and machines**, ultrasound is used to detect internal defects. The waves are passed through the **metal block** and detected by sensors; if there is a crack, the waves are reflected back, revealing the flaw. ***Hence, this is a correct application.***
 
• **Imaging of internal organs**: **Ultrasonography** is a diagnostic medical technique used to visualize internal organs such as the **liver, kidneys, and uterus**. It helps doctors detect abnormalities like **stones** or **tumors**. ***Hence, this is a correct application.***
 
• **Cooking food**: This is **not** an application of ultrasound. Cooking generally utilizes **thermal energy** (conduction, convection, radiation) or **Microwaves**, which are **electromagnetic waves** that vibrate water molecules to produce heat. Ultrasound is a **mechanical wave** and does not possess the thermal properties required for standard cooking. ***Hence, statement 1 is the correct answer as it is NOT an application.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Medical Applications (Echocardiography)**:

 
 
• **Echocardiography** is a specific use of ultrasound to capture images of the **heart** and its movements, used to diagnose **cardiac diseases**.
 
• Another medical use is **Lithotripsy**, where high-energy ultrasound waves are employed to break **kidney stones** into small grains that can be passed out through urine.
 
 
 
• **Industrial and Marine Uses (SONAR)**:
 
 
• **SONAR (Sound Navigation and Ranging)** utilizes ultrasound to measure the **depth of the ocean** and to locate underwater objects like **submarines, icebergs, or sunken ships**.
 
• The **echo-ranging** principle is used here, where the time interval between transmission and reception of the pulse is recorded to calculate **distance**.
 
 
 
• **Biological Use (Echolocation)**:
 
 
• Animals like **bats, dolphins, and porpoises** emit ultrasound waves to navigate and detect prey in the dark.
 
• **Bats** can produce frequencies up to **100 kHz** to create a "sound map" of their surroundings.
 
 
 
• **Physical Properties**:
 
 
• Ultrasound waves have a **short wavelength**, allowing them to penetrate deep into materials and reflect off very small surfaces, making them ideal for **non-destructive testing** and **high-resolution imaging**.

questions.question: What happens when we dissolve sugar in water?

options.text: The particles of sugar will float on top of water.
The particles of sugar get into the spaces between particles of water.
The particles of sugar and water do not mix.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The particles of sugar get into the spaces between particles of water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Everything around us is made of **matter**, which is composed of extremely tiny **particles**. These particles are so small that they cannot be seen with the naked eye.
 
• One of the fundamental characteristics of matter is that there are **intermolecular spaces** between the particles. In liquids like **water**, these spaces are larger than in solids but smaller than in gases.
 
• When **sugar** (the **solute**) is added to **water** (the **solvent**) and stirred, the sugar crystals break down into individual **molecules**.
 
• These sugar molecules then distribute themselves uniformly throughout the liquid by occupying the **empty spaces** or **voids** between the water particles. ***Hence, the statement that particles of sugar get into the spaces between particles of water is correct.***
 
• The sugar particles do not simply float on top because they are **denser** than water and, once dissolved, they form a uniform mixture. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• A **colloidal solution** is a mixture where the particle size is between **1 to 1000 nanometers** and exhibits the **Tyndall effect**. Sugar in water forms a **true solution**, where particles are smaller than **1 nm**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Sugar is highly **soluble** in water due to the formation of **hydrogen bonds** between sugar molecules and water molecules, meaning they mix thoroughly. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **True Solution:** A **true solution** is a **homogeneous mixture** of two or more substances. In this case, the sugar solution is clear, transparent, and the components cannot be separated by **filtration**.
 
• **Solute and Solvent:** In a solution, the substance that is dissolved is called the **solute** (e.g., **sugar**), and the substance in which it is dissolved is the **solvent** (e.g., **water**).
 
• **Conservation of Volume:** Interestingly, when a small amount of sugar is dissolved in water, the overall **volume** of the liquid does not increase significantly. This is a classic experiment used in **General Science** to prove that matter has spaces between its particles.
 
• **Saturation:** A solution is called a **saturated solution** when no more solute can be dissolved in the solvent at a specific **temperature**. If more sugar is added beyond this point, it will settle at the bottom.
 
• **Kinetic Theory:** The particles of matter are in **continuous motion**. This constant movement helps the sugar particles **diffuse** and spread evenly throughout the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Effect of Temperature:** The **solubility** of sugar in water increases with an increase in **temperature**. This is because higher temperatures provide more **kinetic energy**, which increases the **vibration** of water molecules and expands the **intermolecular spaces**, allowing more sugar to fit in.
 
• **Physical Change:** Dissolving sugar in water is considered a **physical change** because no new chemical substance is formed; the sugar can be recovered by the process of **evaporation** or **crystallization**.
 
• **Particle Size:** In a sugar solution, the particles are less than **10⁻⁹ meters** (or **1 nm**) in diameter, which is why they do not scatter a beam of light.
 
• **Concentration:** The amount of sugar present in a given amount of solution is known as its **concentration**, which can be expressed in terms of **molarity**, **molality**, or **mass percentage**.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the process of sexual maturation in humans?

options.text: It begins after adulthood and leads to immediate readiness for parenthood
It occurs only in females and stops once menstruation begins
It is a gradual process during adolescence involving physical and hormonal changes
It occurs suddenly and marks the end of body growth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is a gradual process during adolescence involving physical and hormonal changes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sexual maturation, commonly known as **puberty**, is the biological process by which a child's body matures into an adult body capable of sexual reproduction.
 
• Sexual maturation does not begin after adulthood; rather, it is the bridge that leads to **adulthood**, typically starting between the ages of **10 and 12 years**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• This process occurs in both **males and females**. While the specific physical changes differ between the sexes, both undergo significant hormonal and physiological shifts. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• It is characterized as a **gradual process** that spans several years during the period of **adolescence**. It involves the complex interaction of the **nervous system** and the **endocrine system** to trigger growth and development. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Sexual maturation is not a sudden or overnight event. It involves a series of stages (often measured by the **Tanner scale**) and does not mark the immediate end of body growth; in fact, a significant **growth spurt** occurs during this phase. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• During this period, the **gonads** (testes in males and ovaries in females) begin to produce **gametes** and secrete sex **hormones**, leading to the development of **secondary sexual characteristics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hormonal Regulation:**

 
 
• The process is initiated by the **hypothalamus**, which releases **Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH)**.
 
• This stimulates the **pituitary gland** to secrete **Luteinizing Hormone (LH)** and **Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH)**.
 
• In males, these hormones stimulate the **testes** to produce **testosterone** and **sperm**.
 
• In females, they stimulate the **ovaries** to produce **estrogen** and **progesterone**, leading to **ovulation**.
 
 
 
• **Changes in Females:**
 
 
• The first sign is usually **breast development** (thelarche), followed by the growth of **pubic hair**.
 
• **Menarche**, the first menstrual period, typically occurs about **two years** after the start of breast development, usually around age **12 to 13**.
 
• There is also a widening of the **pelvis** and increased deposition of **fat** in the hips and thighs.
 
 
 
• **Changes in Males:**
 
 
• The first sign is the **enlargement of the testes**, followed by the growth of **pubic hair** and **facial hair**.
 
• The **larynx** (voice box) enlarges, causing the **voice to deepen**.
 
• Males experience increased **muscle mass** and a significant increase in height during their **growth spurt**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Adolescence:** The **World Health Organization (WHO)** defines adolescence as the period of life between **10 and 19 years** of age. It is a critical phase of physical, psychological, and social transition.
 
• **Secondary Sexual Characteristics:** These are features that appear during **puberty** which distinguish the two sexes of a species, but which are not directly part of the **reproductive system** (e.g., facial hair in men, breasts in women).
 
• **Primary Sexual Characteristics:** These refer to the **genitals** and internal reproductive organs (testes, ovaries, uterus) that are present at birth but mature during **sexual maturation**.
 
• **Environmental Factors:** The timing of sexual maturation can be influenced by **genetics**, **nutrition**, and overall health. Improved nutrition globally has led to a historical trend of earlier onset of **puberty**.
