questions.question: What does the seed contain that is essential for the growth of a new plant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Embryo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Embryo** is the most vital part of a **seed** as it is the "baby plant" that contains the potential to grow into a new individual. It consists of the **plumule** (the embryonic shoot) and the **radicle** (the embryonic root). ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Chlorophyll** is the green pigment located in the **chloroplasts** of plant cells, primarily in the **leaves** and **stems**. While it is essential for **photosynthesis**, it is not the structural component within a seed that initiates the growth of a new plant; rather, it is synthesized as the seedling develops. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• A **Sepal** is a part of the **flower whorl** (the calyx) that functions to protect the **flower bud** before it blooms. It is an external floral organ and is not a component found inside a seed. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Nectar** is a sugar-rich liquid secreted by plants in **nectaries** to attract **pollinators** such as **bees**, **birds**, and **bats**. It plays a role in **pollination** and **reproduction** but is not stored inside the seed for the growth of the new plant. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• A **seed** essentially consists of three main parts: the **seed coat**, the **embryo**, and the **endosperm** (or cotyledons) which provides **nutrition** during the initial stages of **germination**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of the Seed Embryo**:

 
 
• The **Radicle** is the first part of the embryo to emerge during **germination**, eventually forming the **primary root** system to absorb **water** and **nutrients**.
 
• The **Plumule** develops into the **shoot system**, producing the first true **leaves** of the plant.
 
• The **Hypocotyl** is the region of the embryo between the radicle and the **cotyledons**, which helps push the seed upward through the **soil**.
 
 
 
• **Nutritional Support**:
 
 
• **Cotyledons**, also known as **seed leaves**, store **food** (starch, proteins, and fats) to sustain the embryo until it can perform **photosynthesis**.
 
• In **monocots** (like **Maize**), there is only **one cotyledon**, while in **dicots** (like **Beans**), there are **two cotyledons**.
 
 
 
• **Seed Coat (Testa)**:
 
 
• The **seed coat** is the hard outer covering that protects the delicate **embryo** from **mechanical injury**, **desiccation**, and **pathogens**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Germination Factors**: For the **embryo** to begin growing, specific environmental conditions must be met, including the presence of **moisture (water)**, **oxygen** for **respiration**, and a suitable **temperature**.
 
• **Dormancy**: Many seeds undergo a period of **dormancy**, a state of **metabolic inactivity** that prevents the embryo from germinating until conditions are favorable for survival, often triggered by **seasonal changes** or **hormonal levels** like **Abscisic Acid**.
 
• **Seed Dispersal**: Plants have evolved various **mechanisms** to disperse seeds, such as **wind** (Anemochory), **water** (Hydrochory), and **animals** (Zoochory), ensuring the **embryo** can find a suitable **location** to grow away from the parent plant.

questions.question: What is the function of salivary amylase present in human saliva?

options.text: It converts amino acids into protein.
It converts simple sugars into starch.
It converts starch into simple sugars.
It converts proteins into amino acids.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It converts starch into simple sugars**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Salivary amylase**, also known as **ptyalin**, is a digestive enzyme present in **human saliva** that initiates the process of chemical digestion in the **mouth**.
 
• The primary function of this enzyme is to catalyze the **hydrolysis** of **starch** (a complex polysaccharide) into smaller, simpler sugars like **maltose**, **maltotriose**, and **limit dextrins**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Statement 1 suggests the conversion of **amino acids** into **protein**. This is a synthetic (anabolic) process known as **translation** that occurs within the **ribosomes** of cells, not in the digestive tract. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 2 refers to the conversion of **simple sugars** into **starch**. This is a process of **polymerization** typically performed by **plants** to store energy; humans store excess sugar as **glycogen** in the liver and muscles. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 4 describes the conversion of **proteins** into **amino acids**. This task is performed by **proteolytic enzymes** such as **pepsin** in the stomach and **trypsin** or **chymotrypsin** in the small intestine. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• About **30% of starch** is hydrolyzed in the oral cavity by salivary amylase before the food is swallowed into the **esophagus**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Composition of Saliva:** Human **saliva** is composed of approximately **99.5% water** and **0.5% solutes**, including **electrolytes** (sodium, potassium, chloride), **mucus**, **antibacterial agents** (lysozyme), and **digestive enzymes**.
 
• **Salivary Glands:** There are three major pairs of **salivary glands**: the **parotid** (located near the ears), **submandibular** (below the jaw), and **sublingual** (under the tongue). These glands produce between **1 and 1.5 liters** of saliva every day.
 
• **Enzymatic Action:** Salivary amylase requires **chloride ions** as activators to function effectively. It specifically targets the **alpha-1,4-glycosidic bonds** in starch molecules.
 
• **pH Sensitivity:** The enzyme works best at an **optimum pH of 6.8**. When the food (bolus) reaches the **stomach**, the highly acidic **gastric juice** (pH 1.5 to 3.5) **denatures** the salivary amylase, halting carbohydrate digestion until it reaches the small intestine.
 
• **Digestion Stages:** Digestion is broadly divided into **mechanical digestion** (mastication or chewing) and **chemical digestion** (enzymatic breakdown). Saliva facilitates both by **lubricating** the food and providing the necessary enzymes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pancreatic Amylase:** Since food spends very little time in the mouth, most starch digestion is completed in the **small intestine** by **pancreatic amylase**, which is secreted by the **pancreas** into the **duodenum**.
 
• **Role of Lysozyme:** Saliva also contains **lysozyme**, which acts as an **antimicrobial agent** by attacking the cell walls of certain **bacteria**, helping to prevent infections and tooth decay.
 
• **Glucose Absorption:** The end product of total carbohydrate digestion is **glucose**, which is absorbed into the **bloodstream** through the **villi** of the small intestine to provide **ATP** (energy) to the body cells.
 
• **Biological Catalyst:** Enzymes like amylase are **biological catalysts** that speed up chemical reactions without being consumed in the process, allowing digestion to occur rapidly at **body temperature (37°C)**.

• **Sir Isaac Newton** was the first to use a **glass prism** to obtain the spectrum of sunlight. He observed that when a narrow beam of sunlight falls on a prism, it splits into a band of seven colors.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles do NOT have their own DNA?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lysosomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the **Golgi apparatus**. They contain **hydrolytic enzymes** but do **not** possess their own **DNA** or **ribosomes**.
 
• The **Nucleus** is the most essential part of a **eukaryotic cell**, acting as the control center. It contains the majority of the cell's **genetic material** in the form of **DNA** molecules organized into **chromosomes**.
 
• **Mitochondria** are known as **semi-autonomous organelles** because they contain their own **circular DNA**, **RNA**, and **70S ribosomes**, allowing them to synthesize some of their own **proteins**.
 
• **Plastids**, found in all **plant cells** and **euglenoids**, also possess their own **double-stranded circular DNA** and **ribosomes**. Similar to mitochondria, they can replicate independently of the nucleus.
 
• Among the given options, only **Lysosomes** lack a genome, as their primary function is **intracellular digestion** rather than energy production or genetic storage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes:**

 
 
• These are often referred to as the **"suicidal bags"** of the cell because if the cell gets damaged, lysosomes may burst and the **enzymes** digest their own cell.
 
• They are rich in almost all types of **hydrolytic enzymes** (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) optimally active at the **acidic pH**.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria:**
 
 
• Commonly called the **"Powerhouse of the cell,"** they are the sites of **aerobic respiration** and produce cellular energy in the form of **ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate).
 
• The presence of **mtDNA** (Mitochondrial DNA) supports the **Endosymbiotic Theory**, which suggests they originated from **prokaryotic cells**.
 
 
 
• **Plastids:**
 
 
• Based on the type of **pigments**, plastids can be classified into **chloroplasts**, **chromoplasts**, and **leucoplasts**.
 
• **Chloroplasts** contain **chlorophyll** and **carotenoid pigments** which are responsible for trapping light energy essential for **photosynthesis**.
 
 
 
• **Organelle Autonomy:**
 
 
• Organelles like the **Nucleus**, **Mitochondria**, and **Chloroplasts** (a type of plastid) are **double-membrane bound**, whereas **Lysosomes** are **single-membrane bound**.
 
• The **DNA** found in mitochondria and plastids is **circular**, resembling **bacterial DNA**, while **nuclear DNA** is typically **linear**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Genetic Material Location:** In a typical **animal cell**, **DNA** is strictly confined to the **nucleus** and the **mitochondria**. In **plant cells**, it is found in the **nucleus**, **mitochondria**, and **plastids**.
 
• **Ribosomes:** While **ribosomes** themselves contain **RNA**, they are not considered organelles that "have" DNA; rather, they are the machinery that translates **genetic information**.
 
• **Prokaryotic Cells:** Unlike eukaryotes, **prokaryotes** do not have membrane-bound organelles like **mitochondria** or **lysosomes**; their **DNA** is found in a region called the **nucleoid**.

questions.question: The mechanical energy of a body can be expressed as the sum of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**potential energy and kinetic energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Mechanical energy** is defined as the energy possessed by an object due to its **motion** or its **stored energy of position**. It is a **macroscopic** form of energy.

questions.question: A positive number when increased by 14, equals 176 times its reciprocal. What is the number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We can solve this quickly by verifying the given options.

Let's test the number 8.

The number increased by 14 = 8 + 14 = 22.

176 times the reciprocal of 8 = 176 × (1/8) = 22.

Since both conditions match perfectly, the required number must be 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A positive number when increased by 14 is equal to 176 times its reciprocal.

**Calculations:**

Let the positive number be x.

⇒ x + 14 = 176 × (1/x)

Multiplying the entire equation by x:

⇒ x(x + 14) = 176

⇒ x² + 14x = 176

⇒ x² + 14x − 176 = 0

Now, we factorise the quadratic equation:

⇒ x² + 22x − 8x − 176 = 0

⇒ x(x + 22) − 8(x + 22) = 0

⇒ (x − 8)(x + 22) = 0

⇒ x = 8 or x = −22

Since the question states it is a positive number, we discard −22.

⇒ x = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Form of a Quadratic Equation

A quadratic equation is generally expressed as ax² + bx + c = 0, where a, b, and c are constants, and a is not equal to 0.

Sum and Product of Roots

If α and β are roots of the quadratic equation, then Sum of roots (α + β) = −b/a and Product of roots (α × β) = c/a.

Discriminant and Nature of Roots

The discriminant D = b² − 4ac determines the nature of roots. If D > 0, the roots are real and distinct; if D = 0, the roots are real and equal; if D < 0, the roots are imaginary.

• This move is aimed at strictly monitoring the quality of imported jute and ensuring that **anti-dumping regulations** are effectively enforced to protect domestic manufacturers. ***Hence, the option Bangladesh is correct.***
 
• Prior to this, a significant volume of jute entered India through land border crossings in **West Bengal**, such as **Petrapole**, but the new mandate redirects all traffic to a single maritime gateway for better oversight.
 
• The restriction is expected to impact the supply chain of the Indian **jute industry**, which relies on high-quality fiber from **Bangladesh** to supplement domestic production.
 
• Other neighboring countries like **Pakistan**, **Nepal**, and **China** do not have similar port-specific restrictions for jute in this specific **June 2025** directive. ***Hence, these options are incorrect.***

• This certification scheme ensures that hydrogen production meets the specific "Green" standards, which require that carbon emissions do not exceed **2 kg CO2 equivalent per kg of hydrogen** produced.

• The scheme is overseen by the **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)**, which acts as the nodal ministry for implementing the mission's objectives and coordinating with the **Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE)**.

• The mission aims to develop a green hydrogen production capacity of at least **5 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT)** per annum by the year **2030**.
 
• It seeks to add about **125 Gigawatts (GW)** of renewable energy capacity to the country's grid specifically for hydrogen production.
 
• The mission is expected to reduce **fossil fuel imports** by over **₹1 lakh crore** and abate nearly **50 MMT** of annual greenhouse gas emissions by **2030**.
 
 
 
• **Green India Initiative**:
 
 
• This is part of the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)**, primarily focused on **afforestation**, protecting **biodiversity**, and increasing **forest cover** across **India**.
 
 
 
• **National Solar Energy Mission**:
 
 
• Launched in **January 2010**, it is a major initiative to promote **solar power** and establish **India** as a global leader in solar energy by creating policy conditions for its diffusion across the country.

• **Well-to-Gate Scope**: The certification follows a **well-to-gate** boundary, encompassing water treatment, electrolysis, gas purification, drying, and compression of hydrogen.

• The **Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve**, located in the state of **Himachal Pradesh**, was inducted into the **UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves (WNBR)** in **September 2025**.
 
• This reserve spans across the **Spiti Valley** and includes significant protected areas such as the **Pin Valley National Park**, **Chandertal**, and **Sarchu**.
 
• It is characterized by its high-altitude **trans-Himalayan** ecosystem, featuring extreme cold temperatures and arid conditions, which support a unique variety of flora and fauna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves (WNBR):**
 
 
• The **WNBR** is an international network created by **UNESCO** under the **Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme** launched in **1971**.
 
• It seeks to establish a scientific basis for the improvement of relationships between people and their environments, promoting the **conservation of biodiversity** and **sustainable use** of resources.
 
 
 
• **Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve:**

• It includes **Satpura National Park** and serves as a transition zone between the **Deccan Plateau** and the **Gangetic Plains**.
 
 
 
• **Achanakmar-Amarkantak Biosphere Reserve:**
 
 
• This reserve covers parts of **Chhattisgarh** and **Madhya Pradesh**. It was included in the **UNESCO** list in **2012**.
 
• It is known for being the source of the **Narmada**, **Johilla**, and **Son Rivers** and features diverse topography from hills to plains.
 
 
 
• **Kachchh Biosphere Reserve:**
 
 
• Situated in **Gujarat**, it is the largest Biosphere Reserve in **India** by area.
 
• It is famous for the **Great Rann of Kutch** and provides a sanctuary for the **Indian Wild Ass** (Khur) and several migratory birds like **Flamingos**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• The first Biosphere Reserve to be established in **India** was the **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve** in **1986**, which was also the first to join the **UNESCO** list in **2000**.
 
• **Biosphere Reserves** are divided into three zones: the **Core Area** (strictly protected), the **Buffer Zone** (used for research and education), and the **Transition Area** (where sustainable human activities occur).
 
• The designation of these sites helps in implementing the **Convention on Biological Diversity** and the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** set by the **United Nations**.

__
 
• The **Union Budget 2025–26** was presented in the **Parliament** of India by the **Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman** on **February 1, 2025**.
 
• For the financial year **2025-26**, the **Fiscal Deficit** is estimated to be **4.4% of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**. This target is a significant milestone in the government's **fiscal consolidation** roadmap.
 
• This estimate follows the **Revised Estimate (RE)** of the previous financial year (2024-25), where the fiscal deficit was pegged at **4.9%**. The reduction to **4.4%** demonstrates a disciplined approach to managing the **national debt**.
 
• The government had previously set a target in the **2021-22 Budget** to reach a fiscal deficit level below **4.5% of GDP** by the year **2025-26**. By setting the target at **4.4%**, the government has successfully stayed ahead of its projected trajectory.
 
• The fiscal deficit represents the difference between the **Total Expenditure** of the government and its **Total Receipts** (excluding borrowings). A deficit of **4.4%** indicates the extent to which the government must borrow to fund its operations and investments.

• A lower fiscal deficit generally leads to lower **inflation** and lower interest rates, which encourages **private investment**.

• The **multiplier effect** of Capex is essential for sustaining long-term **Economic Growth** and job creation.

questions.question: Which of the following schemes was launched by the Gujarat government in May 2025 that sends real-time SMS alerts to citizens about their police case progress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I-Pragati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of Gujarat** launched the **I-Pragati** scheme in **May 2025** to revolutionize citizen-police interactions through technology.
 
• The **I-Pragati** system is designed to provide **real-time SMS alerts** to complainants regarding the status and progress of their police cases, ensuring they stay informed without manual follow-ups.
 
• Under this scheme, citizens receive automated notifications for various stages of the legal process, including the **registration of an FIR**, the **appointment of an Investigating Officer (IO)**, and the **submission of the charge sheet** or final report in court. ***Hence, the option I-Pragati is correct.***
 
• The initiative aims to enhance **transparency**, **accountability**, and **public trust** by bridging the communication gap between the **Gujarat Police** and the general public.
 
• By utilizing the **CCTNS (Crime and Criminal Tracking Network & Systems)** database, the system automatically triggers messages to the registered **mobile number** of the victim or complainant as soon as an update is entered into the police records.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **e-FIR Service in Gujarat:**
 
 
• Prior to **I-Pragati**, **Gujarat** had already established a robust digital framework, including an **e-FIR** portal for reporting **mobile phone** and **vehicle thefts** online.
 
• This service allows citizens to file complaints for specific non-heinous crimes through a **web portal** or **mobile application**, reducing the footfall at physical **police stations**.
 
 
 
• **CCTNS Project:**
 
 
• The **Crime and Criminal Tracking Network & Systems (CCTNS)** is a **National e-Governance** initiative aimed at creating a nationwide integrated system for sharing **real-time crime data** across different states.
 
• In **Gujarat**, the high level of **CCTNS implementation** has enabled the integration of various citizen-centric services like **I-Pragati**.
 
 
 
• **VISWAS Project:**
 
 
• The **Video Integration and State Wide Advanced Security (VISWAS)** is another major project by the **Gujarat Government**.
 
• It involves the installation of over **7,000 CCTV cameras** across **33 districts** for traffic management, crime prevention, and detection.
 
 
 
• **Digital India and Gujarat:**
 
 
• **Gujarat** consistently ranks high in **e-governance** indices in **India**, implementing various digital solutions like the **Pocket Cop** project, which provides **smartphones** to police officers for instant verification of **criminal records** and **passport verifications**.

• The introduction of **SMS alerts** helps in curbing **corruption** and **delays** by making the police process more visible to the public.
 
• It specifically benefits individuals in **rural areas** who previously had to travel long distances to **district headquarters** or **police stations** just to inquire about their case status.
 
• The **I-Pragati** scheme reflects the **"Minimum Government, Maximum Governance"** philosophy by automating administrative communications.
